title: DEA registration on discontinuance or transfer of a business
subtopic: Federal registration on closure or transfer of ownership
rule_summary: A DEA registration TERMINATES without further action when the registrant dies, ceases legal existence, discontinues business or professional practice, or surrenders the registration, and a registrant who ceases legal existence or discontinues business shall notify the Administrator promptly. NO REGISTRATION OR ANY AUTHORITY CONFERRED BY IT MAY BE ASSIGNED OR OTHERWISE TRANSFERRED except on conditions the Administration designates and only pursuant to WRITTEN CONSENT, on a written request giving full details. A registrant discontinuing business activities altogether or as to controlled substances WITHOUT transferring them to another person shall RETURN ITS CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION AND ANY UNEXECUTED ORDER FORMS FOR CANCELLATION to the DEA Registration Unit, and may dispose of the controlled substances in its possession in accordance with 21 CFR part 1317. A registrant discontinuing BY TRANSFERRING the business to another person shall submit IN PERSON OR BY REGISTERED OR CERTIFIED MAIL, RETURN RECEIPT REQUESTED, to the Special Agent in Charge for its area, AT LEAST 14 DAYS IN ADVANCE of the proposed transfer UNLESS THE SPECIAL AGENT IN CHARGE WAIVES that limitation, the names, addresses, registration numbers and authorized business activities of transferor and transferee, whether the activities continue at the registered location or move, whether the transferor holds a Schedule I or II quota, and the date the transfer of controlled substances will occur. Unless the Special Agent in Charge tells the transferor before that date that the transfer may not occur, the transferor may distribute the controlled substances to the transferee without being registered to distribute, provided that ON THE DATE OF TRANSFER a complete inventory of all controlled substances being transferred is taken under 21 CFR 1304.11, which SERVES AS THE FINAL INVENTORY OF THE TRANSFEROR AND THE INITIAL INVENTORY OF THE TRANSFEREE with a copy in each person's records and need not be filed with the Administration unless the Special Agent in Charge requests it; that transfers of Schedule I or II substances USE ORDER FORMS under 21 CFR part 1305; and that the part 1304 records for the substances transferred pass to the transferee on that date, custody and maintenance becoming the transferee's responsibility while accuracy before the transfer remains the transferor's.
exam_relevance: Tests the federal steps that run alongside a Massachusetts closure or sale: the buyer needs its own registration because a DEA registration is not assignable, the transferor owes the Special Agent in Charge 14 days' advance notice, and one transfer-date inventory closes one registrant's books and opens the other's.

authority.name: Termination of registration; transfer of registration; distribution upon discontinuance of business

numeric_facts.fact: Advance notice to the DEA Special Agent in Charge before transferring a business with its controlled substances
numeric_facts.conditions: in person or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, unless the Special Agent in Charge waives the period

exceptions: The Special Agent in Charge may waive the 14-day advance-notice period in individual instances.
The transfer-date inventory need not be filed with the Administration unless the Special Agent in Charge requests it.
common_confusions: Treating a DEA registration as passing with the business: it may not be assigned or transferred except pursuant to the Administration's written consent.

Confusing the two discontinuance routes: a registrant that does not transfer its business returns the certificate and unexecuted order forms for cancellation and disposes of its stock under 21 CFR part 1317.
Forgetting that Schedule I and II stock still moves on order forms even though the transferor is not registered to distribute.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of 21 CFR 1301.52 on the eCFR, displaying title 21 as of 9/10/2026, on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
